No competent alternative reading is supported.
semantic_adjudication.violated_obligation: OperationalControls (an initial pseudostate owner) must have at most one/exactly one default entry transition, per UML §14.5.6.2.

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text root block: 'state InitialState named ...; [*] -> InitialState;' is the only root initial edge; exact_source_inventory tr_0001 source=@initial:__root__ target=InitialState; inspection_equivalent_facts states show CollisionDetection/CollisionAvoidance reachable_from_initial=false and InitialState reachable_from_initial=true with outgoing_transition_refs=[].
issues.expected: The root/enclosing scope's initial pseudostate edge must (directly or via a reachable path) enter CollisionDetection/CollisionAvoidance so the sub-machine can activate on the named detection events.
issues.observed: The exact root-level initial edge (tr_0001 / '[*] -> InitialState;') only targets InitialState, a leaf with zero outgoing transitions; there is no root-owned edge to CollisionDetection or CollisionAvoidance, so the owner scope never enters the sub-machine.
issues.reason: The contract's owner hint (root/enclosing state machine) requires an entry into the collision-avoidance sub-machine; the only closed-model root-owned initial edge goes to InitialState, which is a dead-end, meaning the owner-local entry to the sub-machine is exactly missing, not merely a deeper reachability artifact.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: CollisionDetection -> CollisionAvoidance (guarded by R45RouteToken==15) and CollisionAvoidance -> InitialState (guarded by R45RouteToken==16) exist as cross-composite transitions, suggesting an intended cycle; however neither edge is reachable because nothing enters CollisionDetection or CollisionAvoidance from the root initial edge, so this rebuttal does not establish satisfaction.
issues.title: Root scope has no default/initial edge reaching CollisionDetection or CollisionAvoidance

issues.expected: CollisionDetection and CollisionAvoidance must be reachable from the root initial entry so detection events can actually flow through PossibleCollision, the Collision_Mode_Active handoff, and CollisionAvoidance's regions.
issues.observed: The deterministic reachable-state set for the closed FCSTM is exactly {root wrapper, InitialState}; CollisionDetection, CollisionAvoidance, and every descendant state are marked reachable_from_initial=false, and finite reachability checks for both composites are refuted.
issues.reason: Beyond the owner-local initial-entry gap, the deterministic inventory closes a stronger fact: with only InitialState reachable, the entire detection/avoidance/resolution structure -- including all three named detection events -- is isolated from the root. This is the global reachability consequence that the initial-entry contract alone does not fully state.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: The presence of the cross-composite Collision_Mode_Active/Collision_Resolved edges plus per-region initial edges could be read as evidence of an intended operational cycle whose entry the author simply omitted from the root; this supports treating the defect as one owner-entry gap rather than two separate obligations, but the deterministic non-proved reachability rows for both composites independently establish the unreachable fact regardless of that reading.

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts state_ref state:CollisionAvoidance:line:31 reachable_from_initial=false; fcstm_model.text CollisionAvoidance block comment enumerating 3 populated concurrent regions (region 1: AutomaticBraking/BrakingComplete; region 2: SteeringControl/SteeringComplete; region 3: AlertSystem/AlertComplete).
issues.expected: The orthogonal regions inside CollisionAvoidance (AutomaticBraking/BrakingComplete, SteeringControl/SteeringComplete, AlertSystem/AlertComplete) must be able to concurrently and ongoingly activate their respective collision-avoidance controls.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidance itself is unreachable from the root initial entry (reachable_from_initial=false), so none of its three populated concurrent regions can ever begin executing; the frozen predicate registry has no direct construct for a concurrent-progress/ongoing-activation claim of this kind.
issues.reason: This is a precise semantic claim (ongoing concurrent activation of collision-avoidance controls) with no exact frozen predicate expressing multi-region ongoing-progress; it must remain a W1 candidate rather than being silently dropped, and is grounded in the same unreachable-composite fact used for the derived reachability contract without collapsing the two properties.
issues.requirement_quote: allow for concurrent activation different of collision avoidance controls
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each region does have an internal default initial edge to its first state (AutomaticBraking/SteeringControl/AlertSystem) and an exit edge back out via Collision_Resolved, which is locally well-formed concurrent structure; if CollisionAvoidance were reached, the regions would operate correctly, so the defect is purely upstream reachability rather than a defect intrinsic to the region_structure/state_action modeling itself.

issues.expected: The root/enclosing machine must enter CollisionAvoidance upon a collision-detection event, i.e. a reachable owner-level path from root through CollisionDetection's detection/consumption transitions into CollisionAvoidance must exist.
issues.observed: The only owned root-level transition realized in reachable state is `[*] -> InitialState` (transition:line:62), which bypasses CollisionDetection and CollisionAvoidance entirely. CollisionDetection, its four detection states, and CollisionAvoidance are all marked reachable_from_initial=false, and the CollisionDetection->CollisionAvoidance edge (transition:line:60, guarded by R45RouteToken==15) is itself unreachable, so CollisionAvoidance can never become active in the closed model regardless of which collision event fires.
issues.reason: The owner (root machine) fails to reach the collision-avoidance activation path at all; this is a root-reachability failure of the exact owner->target activation obligation, independent from the local nested initial edges inside CollisionDetection/CollisionAvoidance which are individually well-formed.
issues.requirement_quote: This sub-machine becomes active when a possible frontend collision, rear-end collision or collision with pedestrian is detected.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A source-authored `CollisionDetection -> CollisionAvoidance` edge and a nested `[*] -> PossibleCollision` initial edge do exist in the exact source/model inventory, so the intended activation path is structurally present; the defect is that the root-level default entry routes only to InitialState instead of CollisionDetection, not that the sub-machine's own internal entry is malformed.
issues.title: CollisionAvoidance sub-machine is never entered from root; only a stray InitialState default edge is reachable
